newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn says revaluing gold could impact 97 budget.
newsitem.headline: Bonn says revaluing gold could impact 97 budget.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry on Friday said revaluing the Bundesbank's gold could have an impact on the country's 1997 budget if the central bank made an interim account this year.
"There are a range of possibilities, for example, by making an interim account," a Finance Ministry spokeswoman told a regular government news conference.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel, faced with an 18 billion mark ($10.6 billion) tax revenue shortfall, said on Thursday that if gold reserves were revalued from current low book prices to levels close to the normal market price it could help close the gap.

A revaluation would effectively deliver Bonn a windfall profit, allowing it to retire old debt more quickly than otherwise. But Waigel has played down this aspect of the changes, selling it instead as a technical move to prepare for the euro currency.

Waigel said on Thursday the revaluation of the gold would not contribute to the reduction of the current deficit, but would help German fulfill the criteria for a single European currency, which the country is struggling to fulfil.
